description: A constructor call with more arguments than declared fields raises `ol-too-many-inputs` (issue #329, `spec/data-structures.md:284`): the parenthesized `(point 3 4 5)` over-supplies the 2-field `point`. The bare `point 3 4 5` form instead groups by arity and leaves a stray token (`ol-bad-token`), identical to how a fixed-arity user procedure reads its arguments — so over-supply is expressed with the same parenthesized form the language uses everywhere else. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
